title: How Shrinkflation Hides a Price Increase

visual_thesis.episode_promise: Reveal how an unchanged shelf price can conceal a higher price per gram and a faster repurchase cycle.
visual_thesis.familiar_situation: A shopper automatically reaches for the same cereal box bought every month.
visual_thesis.decision_moment: The hand checks the large shelf price but passes over the net weight and unit price.
visual_thesis.hidden_mechanism: The familiar package remains the shopper's mental unit while the quantity inside becomes the changing denominator.
visual_thesis.business_gain: A seller can pass through costs or protect margins while preserving a familiar price point and reducing sticker shock.
visual_thesis.viewer_consequence: The shopper pays more per gram and returns to buy the product sooner.
visual_thesis.agency_action: The shopper compares a common unit, tracks the normal package size, and calculates cost per use.
visual_thesis.open_loop_object: The tiny price-per-kilogram number on the shelf label.
visual_thesis.thesis_sentence: A familiar cereal box appears normal until its printed surface peels open to reveal missing quantity, a rising unit price, and a faster purchase loop, showing how value moves away from the shopper while the sticker price stands still.

quality_control: Every scene advances a causal state or resets scale; no purely decorative grocery footage.
The recurring carton retains identical shape, palette, illustration, and material unless a mutable redesign state is explicitly called out.
The $4.99 sticker remains fixed whenever the episode is explaining shrinkflation rather than the visible-price alternative.
The old carton is 500 g and the new carton is 450 g in every appearance.
Money is amber, quantity is cream, evidence is cyan, price increase or hidden loss is red, and viewer agency appears green only from scene-052 onward.
Research numbers are added in compositing, not trusted to image generation.
Study findings remain scoped to the named sample and period; uncertainty is visible in scene-025.
The macro sequence makes downsizing visually small overall and concentrated only in the cited categories.
Legal scenes use neutral rules and disclosure frames, never verdict symbols or claims that shrinking is automatically illegal.
France's notice is explicitly scoped in editorial captions to covered products, large stores, and the two-month display period.
No real brand, retailer interface, government seal, or copied package appears.
Generated microtext is replaced with clean post-production typography.
Opening and closing aisle compositions match closely enough for a visible rewind payoff.
The final agency action compares quantity and unit price without portraying ordinary packages as inherently untrustworthy.
